title: Her new CD, current gigs and how to get club bookings
summary: She describes her live CD from St. Peter's, her monthly jam session at Flushing Town Hall, work at Cleopatra's Needle, plans with Carlo Barile, and how to approach clubs.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Anything coming up in the near future that you’re looking forward to?

Well you know I have my new CD, that, it was a live concert here in New York at St. Peter’s that came out real good, on baritone and flute and I sang for the first time, I sang one of my own tunes. And I just went to Italy to promote that and the gigs I did there were to promote that CD, because it just came out, and actually the release date here is officially January 18 so it’s not even yet. And so what I plan to do is organize as many gigs and tours around that as I possibly can. Because I think it’s a good representation of who I am right now. It has its flaws but so do I and you know, it’s like where I am, so I feel good about that. And so I can’t say exactly right now, I mean I lead a jam session at Flushing Town Hall once a month on Wednesdays and I have a very good rhythm section there and I get to do a lot of playing. We play before we start inviting people up, we play a few tunes, and that’s a stable thing. And I work pretty regularly at Cleopatra’s Needle, that’s uptown. So I’m going to be trying to organize some concerts at some of the clubs. There’s a pianist and organ player from Italy, Carlo Barile who has got a new album of his “Manhattan Suite,” it’s a jazz suite about Manhattan. And he’s going to be coming over here so I’m going to try and work out some clubs for us together, maybe Fat Cat, © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
I’m going to approach Mezzrow and see. Because he’s a very high quality player and we want to try to do this together. So I hope that this year will be, I think it probably will be a fruitful year.
Is that like get on the phone and call this club or do you have a more up to date way that —

Well I know that you’re supposed to have an e press kit, which I really don’t. And it would be nice to have an agent, which I don’t. But I think that the steps that probably for me seem very important to take are (1) sticking your nose in the clubs from time to time, just be on the scene, which I don’t do enough but I know that it’s very important. Maybe sit in, maybe not, but just even just go say hello to people. Then of course contact the clubs either by phone or email and drop your CD and present in some way a sheet of paper that explains your project, and then be willing to go through that awful humiliating processing of calling back and calling back and calling back. And all those things count for a lot.
